The test image shows a corn ear with yellow kernels and dark blue-green mold growing between/around all the kernels. Affected part: seed/pod.

Top candidates based on the dark blue-green color:
1. **Trichoderma_Ear_Rot** - dark blue-green conidia between kernels
2. **Aspergillus_Ear_Rot** - olive-green powdery mold
3. **Penicillium_Ear_Rot** - blue-green mold between kernels (not in class list)

Let me view reference images one at a time, starting with Trichoderma.
This Trichoderma reference matches very well - same dark blue-green mold on yellow kernels. Let me check Aspergillus for comparison.
Aspergillus shows olive/khaki-green dusty mold covering kernels. The test image has darker blue-green mold between kernels, more like Trichoderma. Let me check a few more classes to be thorough.

All 8 views used. Summary of comparisons:

- **Trichoderma_Ear_Rot**: Dark blue-green conidia on and between yellow kernels covering the whole ear — matches test image almost exactly
- **Aspergillus_Ear_Rot**: Olive/khaki-green dusty powder covering kernel surfaces — different color and texture
- **Diplodia_Ear_Rot**: White mycelium from base, no blue-green mold — no match
- **Gibberella_Disease**: Pink/red mold at ear tip — no match
- **Fusarium_Disease**: Whitish-pink mold in patches — no match
- **Common_Smut**: Large white/black galls — no match

The test image shows dense dark blue-green mold growing between all kernels across the whole ear on yellow kernels. This is the hallmark of Trichoderma_Ear_Rot. The first Trichoderma reference (Corn_Disease_26.jpg) is nearly identical.
